name: Stonepath Logistics
full_legal_name: Stonepath Integrated Logistics & Sovereign Transit Authority, Corp.-S
sector: Logistics / Heavy Transit & Sovereign Infrastructure Leasing
sovereign_territory: The Stonepath Transit Sovereignty — not a contiguous territory but a legally recognized network of 340 sovereign transit nodes (depots, tunnels, rail junctions, and aerial docking platforms) distributed across the Meridian 88 corridor, connected by 2,200 kilometers of Stonepath-owned right-of-way designated as sovereign linear territory
founding_story: Stonepath was assembled rather than founded — a 2139 consolidation of eleven failing regional freight operators by logistics financier August Tran-Holloway, who recognized that the collapse of public infrastructure in the early megacity era had created a power vacuum in physical transit. Tran-Holloway did not buy the companies for their assets; he bought them for their right-of-way deeds, easements, and tunnel licenses, then spent four years in corridor courts arguing that a network of sovereign transit infrastructure constituted a sovereign territory under the Meridian 88 Corponation Charter. He won in 2143. The ruling is still contested by seven municipalities and celebrated annually inside Stonepath as 'Right-of-Way Day.'
security_force: The Transit Authority Enforcement Division (TAED) — 12,000 personnel operating across the sovereign node network. TAED functions as both a security force and a customs authority, with legal power to detain, search, and levy tariffs on any cargo or personnel transiting Stonepath sovereign right-of-way. Their armored transit enforcement vehicles — called 'Milestones' — are a common and intimidating sight at corridor freight junctions.
key_detail: Stonepath's most valuable and least visible service is the SEALED MANIFEST program — a premium logistics tier in which cargo is transported with zero documentation, zero scanning, and zero third-party disclosure. Clients pay a 400% premium. Stonepath's sovereign right-of-way status means SEALED MANIFEST shipments cannot be inspected by municipal or corridor authorities. The program is used by every member of the Big 20 and by actors that most Big 20 members would prefer not to be associated with.
relationship_to_big_20: Member of the Big 20. Holds the logistics seat and is in direct rivalry with Kelpline Logistics, which dominates waterway and lake freight while Stonepath controls land and aerial transit. The two corponations maintain a formal freight-sharing treaty that both routinely undermine through subsidiary shell operations. Stonepath is broadly regarded as indispensable — every corponation in the Big 20 uses its infrastructure — which Tran-Holloway's successors leverage as a form of institutional immunity.
full_text: Stonepath Integrated Logistics & Sovereign Transit Authority (STP-S) is the backbone of physical cargo movement in Meridian 88, operating not from a single territory but from a legally sovereign network of 340 transit nodes and 2,200 kilometers of right-of-way scattered across the megacity corridor. Assembled by financier August Tran-Holloway in 2139 and granted sovereign status through a landmark 2143 court ruling, Stonepath generates Φ410 billion annually — the highest revenue of any logistics entity in the corridor — by controlling the physical paths that everything and everyone must eventually use. Its 195,000 direct employees and 600,000 contractors move everything from agricultural bulk freight to defense materiel to the undocumented contents of SEALED MANIFEST containers. The Transit Authority Enforcement Division maintains order across the node network with the authority of a customs state. Within the Big 20, Stonepath is simultaneously trusted by everyone and fully loyal to no one — a position its leadership considers the only rational one for an entity that everyone needs.
